context: The ascending array has n = 10 elements at indices 0 through 9. Pointers i and j mark the left and right boundaries of the current search interval, and m is the current midpoint index. The bar heights show only that the values increase. No specific element values are labeled.
description: The dashed blue box in each panel encloses ten elements. In the left panel, the closed interval [i, j] includes its right endpoint j, which points to the last bar. In the right panel, the half-open interval [i, j) excludes its right endpoint j, which points just past the end of the array. For n = 10, the initialization formulas give j = 9 on the left and j = 10 on the right.

When i = j, the closed interval still contains one element to check, while the half-open interval is empty. When shrinking the interval to the left, the closed interval includes its right endpoint, so set j = m − 1 to exclude m. The half-open interval already excludes its right endpoint, so set j = m. The table gives the four rules shown and adds the while condition, the logical opposite of the stopping condition.

frames.explanation: Each convention requires a matching initialization, loop condition, and pair of boundary updates. The updates at the two ends of a closed interval are symmetric.
frames.title: Interval conventions in binary search

summary: Whether the search interval includes its right endpoint j determines how to initialize j, when to stop the loop, and how to update j when moving the right boundary to the left.
